newsitem.title: CHINA: China aviation chief aboard hijacked plane.
newsitem.headline: China aviation chief aboard hijacked plane.

text.p: China's aviation chief was one of two high-ranking officials aboard an Air China plane that a mentally-ill woman tried to hijack to Taiwan last week, airport officials said on Wednesday.

The woman tried to hijack the Air China Boeing 777 on a flight from Beijing to the southern city of Guangzhou on June 2 and wanted to divert the plane to the Nationalist-ruled island of Taiwan, an official at China's central Wuhan airport said.

The plane, with Chen Guangyi, director of the Civil Aviation Administration of China, and Minister of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation Wu Yi on board, landed in the central city of Wuhan where the hijacker was taken into custody, the official said.
The hijacker had already been overwhelmed by the time the plane touched down in Wuhan, the official said.
She described the would-be hijacker as a mentally-ill woman who wanted the plane to fly to Taiwan, which Beijing regards as a renegade province.
China has foiled at least four attempted hijackings to Taiwan in the past two and a half years.

Twelve planes were hijacked from China to Taiwan between April 1993 and June 1994 and the two sides agreed in late 1994 on terms for the return of hijackers after Beijing conceded Taipei could reserve the right to keep some hijackers if it finds they have valid political or religious motives.
A Taiwan man who hijacked a plane to China last March was sent back last month.
Hijackers in China face a maximum penalty of death.
